dedupe_keys.name: bundesnetzagentur analytical cost model for mobile networks analytisches kostenmodell mobilfunknetz

description: The Bundesnetzagentur's analytical cost model for mobile networks is a bottom-up engineering and economic model of an efficient mobile operator, developed for the German regulator by WIK-Consult from 2011. The agency uses it to set mobile termination rates on a pure long-run incremental cost (pure LRIC) basis, as the European Commission's 2009 termination rate recommendation requires. The model dimensions radio access, backhaul and core networks from traffic and coverage demand, then derives the incremental cost of terminating calls. Reference documents describing the model were published in 2012, with updates in 2014 adding LTE, in 2015 and in 2018, each as PDFs with the consultation comments. Coverage: Germany. Format and access: reference documents in German on the Bundesnetzagentur site, free to read; the model software is not published. Caveats: a regulatory model of a hypothetical efficient operator whose parameters follow German rate decisions; it describes network dimensioning, not the actual networks of Telekom, Vodafone or Telefónica. Simulation uses: cost-based economic appraisal of mobile network investment and interconnection pricing, and a documented reference for radio and core network dimensioning. Related records: the Bundesnetzagentur broadband cost model covers the fixed network, the Arcep mobile cost model is the French equivalent, and pysim5g and the India5G model are open techno-economic simulators.
